cases.name: Mary Beatrice "Mary Bea" Perez
cases.about: She loved to dance.
cases.narrative:
On 4/25/1999, a fisherman discovered her body in a ditch on the last day of the annual citywide celebration. She was clad only in a white Mickey Mouse T-shirt and a single white sock. He abducted her after she wandered from her family during a Fiesta event at Market Square in San Antonio, TX. Her body was so decomposed that the medical examiner could not conclude if she had been sexually assaulted, according to an
autopsy report.

Sells was in San Antonio looking for work with the carnival that
accompanies Fiesta. That night, he and a carnival employee identified in police documents as “Red” found a crying Mary Bea, who said she couldn't find her family, according to court
documents. Sells told investigators that he and Red, who were drunk and on drugs, walked with Mary Bea to a spot near a creek bed behind the Union Stock Yards, a mile and a half from Market Square. There was a blue mattress lying there and Sells passed out on it, he said in his confession. At one point, Sells woke up and saw Red having sex with Mary Bea, he said. He passed out again and woke up to Red giving him oral sex, he said. The two men fought and Red ran off, according to Sells' account. Sells “said he then noticed the little girl sitting on the ground,” a police report states. “He said she was sitting on the ground holding her knees to her chest. He said he walked up behind her and strangled her with his hands.”
cases.disclaimer: CONVICTION

cases.name: Mary Margaret "Peggy" Moran
cases.about: She was a nurse at San Antonio Veterans Administration Hospital.
cases.narrative:
Shortly after midnight, he abducted her from the parking lot of the Audie L. Murphy Memorial Veterans' Hospital in San Antonio, TX, where she worked as a nurse while she was walking to her car. He raped her, stabbed her seven times and left her for dead in a brushy field. Although he was arrested hours after the Peggy's abduction, he refused to tell authorities where he had left Moran's body.

Peggy was too weak to move as she laid nude atop a mound of fire ants for 5 days before being found by searchers. Doctors later said half the blood had drained from her body. Moran suffered from dehydration and pneumonia, in addition to a collapsed lung and losing about two-thirds to three quarters of her blood. Doctors said if she had been found a day earlier, she would have survived.

Moran died on 7/31/1975, the day after she was found.

cases.name: Michelle Hensel
cases.about:
On Christmas morning, one of Michelle Hensel's daughters gave birth to Gizelle Michelle Munoz. Michelle Hensel, struggling for her life at the time, would never meet her newborn granddaughter. Fritz Hensel takes solace that at least one life was saved in his daughter's death. "She donated her liver, two kidneys and her corneas," he said. "One of her kidneys went to
her daughter's father-in-law, and it's my understanding that it started working as soon as it was put in. "It makes me feel like Michelle is going to live on — and within the family," her father said.

Her obituary said, "Michelle was both a mother and a father to her three daughters. They were her world and she was determined to raise them right. She did an excellent job of that as she passed on her goodness, kindness, and unselfishness to them. Everyone who knew Michelle liked her, as she was so full of life as to be infectious."

cases.name: Rebecca Ann "Becky" Pantuso Ibarra
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Becky graduated from Robert E. Lee High School in San Antonio and attended Southwest Texas State University in San Marcos.

Becky assumed many roles and responsibilities throughout her life, as an airlines customer service representative, travel agent, florist, and varsity football team mom. Becky was an exceptional wife, mother, grandmother, aunt, and friend to many who were fortunate enough to have known her. Becky was a self-less, courageous person who relentlessly stood for what she believed in, while often putting the needs of others ahead of her own. Becky sought a special purpose in her life after overcoming stage IV colon cancer over a decade ago, and recently completing the Stephen Ministries training program to counsel others in dire emotional states.

Family was above all her most precious commodity, as she treasured spending time with her grandchildren who affectionately knew her as "Nonni". She also enjoyed living life to its fullest; whether it was taking on new hobbies like Zumba and kick boxing, or frequently venturing to her home away from home at the Texas coast with her husband. She was an invaluable treasure to this world and whose presence will be greatly missed."

cases.name: Ana Alicia Ojeda
cases.about:
Those who knew Ojeda described her as a ‘beautiful soul’ who was ‘full of life.’ “She was a single mom who was working hard to raise her daughter,” said Unise Casillas, Ojeda’s cousin. “Ana was just a happy person. She comes from a large family, and we all want justice for her.” Naomi Cruz says her cousin worked hard to save up enough money for a home. She says Ojeda wanted to give her daughter the best life possible.

Her obituary said, "From a young age, Ana exhibited an extraordinary capacity for love and a zest for life. Her radiant smile and generous spirit were a source of joy to all who knew her. She was a beautiful, devoted, and loving mother, always placing Mariana's happiness and well-being above all else. Her dedication to her daughter was unwavering, and their bond was truly special. Ana's love for her family extended to every aspect of her life, and she cherished the moments spent with loved ones, celebrating the simple pleasures and milestones alike. Her interests reflected her love for life and the joy she found in the everyday. Ana had a talent for making the most of every moment, whether it was a quiet evening at home with Mariana or a lively family gathering. Her laughter was infectious, and her presence had the unique ability to make any situation brighter. Those who knew Ana will remember her as a loving, kind, and selfless person. She touched the lives of many with her unwavering positivity and her ability to see the good in people and circumstances. Ana's legacy is one of love and kindness, and she leaves behind a world that is infinitely better for her having been in it. As we bid farewell to Ana Alicia Ojeda, we hold tight to the memories she gave us, the lessons she taught us, and the love she shared with us. Her spirit will live on in the hearts of those she touched, and her light will continue to guide us through the love we carry for her. Ana's life was a beautiful journey that, although cut short, was lived to the fullest with grace, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to those she held dear. We take solace in knowing that Ana's story does not end with her passing, for she has left an indelible mark on our lives. Her love story will be recounted for generations, and her legacy of kindness will be emulated by all who were fortunate enough to feel the warmth of her embrace. Ana Alicia Ojeda may have left this earthly realm, but her spirit remains a guiding star to all who knew her. As we come together to honor her memory, let us celebrate the extraordinary person she was and the profound impact she had on our lives. Rest in peace, dear Ana, until we meet again."
cases.narrative: On 3/29/2024, a friend reportedly found her dead in her home, lying face-down on the floor. According to the Bexar County Medical Examiner’s Office, Ojeda suffered 'sharp force injuries to her upper body.'

Her family released the following statement:

"Our family is devastated from this tragedy. Jewel Mikayla Garcia was a Wonderful person she had a big heart willing to help anyone in need. We are going to miss her so much. It hurts us to think or imagine what she went through. That morning she texted her grandma that she Loved her with all her heart. She was excited she was going to visit her Dad and grandma. she never made it. We are going to miss her beautiful smile. We know she is in a better place. We ask for continued prayers for her babies and family. Thank you for all the love and support. She was a mommy till the end she made sure to lock her babies in a room before he shot her."

cases.name: Kenya Joy Bland
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Kenya is a graduate of Churchill High School and spent most of her life in San Antonio, Texas with the exception of her college years, where she attended and graduated from Prairie View A & M. At Prairie View, she graduated from the Whitlowe R. Green College of Education with a B.S. in Interdisciplinary Studies. After graduation, she fulfilled her dream of being a teacher, specializing in Reading and Writing. She first taught reading at the George Gervin Academy, and lastly at IDEA Monterrey Park where she was the fourth-grade writing teacher. She deeply loved her students or as she liked to call them her ‘scholars’. Before each school year started, she would spend weeks deciding on the perfect classroom theme to encourage them and give them a joyful environment to learn in.

On June 5, 2001 at age 5 Kenya gave her life to Christ during Vacation Bible School and was baptized on June 10, 2001 at Maranatha Bible Church, where her membership remained until her home going. She stayed active throughout her many years at Maranatha serving in the Cherubim and Youth Choirs, Youth Ministry, Sunday School Ministry, Young Adult Ministry, Mo Ranch, and spoke at special programs like the Mother Daughter Banquet. She also served in The Ark Nursery Ministry where she discovered her passion for teaching. Kenya loved traveling, shopping (especially unique shoes and cute purses), working out, developing her cooking skills, and cherished spending time with family and friends."

cases.name: Stacey Adams Dramiga
cases.about:
She worked at the Brooke Army Medical Center, which released a statement on Wednesday, saying ...“Our heartfelt condolences go out to her family, friends, and co-workers. Stacey was a beloved member of the BAMC staff and will be greatly missed.”

Bexar County Sheriff Javier Salazar held a press conference. Dramiga was a “regular” at the park, he said. “She loved to come walk the Greenway Trails in the morning,” he said.
cases.narrative: The autopsy report said Dramiga died of “blunt force, penetrating trauma of the head,” the Medical Examiner’s Office said.

cases.name: Norma Linda Villarreal
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Norma was a guiding light to all who knew her, embodying compassion, kindness, and a steadfast commitment to her family. Norma loved and tended to her plants and often gifted them to others to share her love; a passion that she learned from her Momma. She also loved the beauty of doves, her nickname was "La Paloma". She thoroughly enjoyed working. Her toils brought her great fulfillment as she worked tirelessly to serve others. Norma could be found dancing to her favorite songs with the biggest, brightest smile on her face. Norma was the heart and soul of her family, bringing joy and warmth to every gathering. She cherished her family, friends, and co-workers, and always treated everyone equally. 

Norma's unwavering support and thoughtfulness made her an irreplaceable figure in the lives of those who loved her. She was the glue that held the family together, always ensuring that everyone was celebrated on their birthdays and had the essentials they needed. Her nurturing spirit and attentiveness to life's details will be sorely missed, but her memory will continue to inspire us all."
